request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of its sheet's descendants, and its claims are generated on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Storing it:** a new migration, `V95__plan_target_sheet.sql`, adds a nullable `target_sheet` column to `plan`. The request, the `Plan` record and `Plans` carry it, and the plan list returns it as `sheet`.
- **Adding a plan (`AddPlan`):** if the sheet field isn't one of this sheet's descendants, the plan is refused with `plan-error` and nothing is saved. A plan with a sheet adds ` sheet=<id>` to the end of its `PLAN_ADDED` line.
- **Generating (`GeneratePlans`):** for a plan with a sheet, claims are made on that sheet for the person with the same name there, and none if there's no such person. The due-by date, payment terms, closed-period checks, late entry, `CLAIM_ADDED`/`LATE_ENTRY` audit lines and rollup all use that sheet. The plan still counts what it made, so `plan-generated` and the "made" count include those claims.
- **Front end:** the plan form has a new `plan-form-sheet` input, and a plan row shows "on sheet <id>" when it has one.

Three choices the request didn't settle:
- A plan's sheet set to its own sheet is refused, since the sheet isn't its own descendant.
- The newest date a plan generates up to is still the plan's own sheet's today. The test depends on this.
- The due-by date and terms use the other sheet's today, since those are part of "that sheet's rules". If you'd rather they use the plan's own sheet's today, it's a one-line change.
